title: Air drag and speed
hook: Change relative speed and predict drag force.
misconception: drag force doubles when relative speed doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply F_d = ½ρC_dAv² to compare drag force when relative speed changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a fixed drag coefficient fluid density and frontal area, F_d = ½ρC_dAv². When relative speed doubles, drag force becomes 4 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model F_d = ½ρC_dAv²; scaling exponent 2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a fixed drag coefficient fluid density and frontal area, with a nonzero initial result. If relative speed triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on drag force?
recall.why: Apply F_d = ½ρC_dAv² under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 9.
